metadata.title: Density Pass 38 -- Hancock Wounded and the Union Command Crisis (Ticks 552-570)
metadata.description: Winfield Scott Hancock — the man who held the Union center together all three days — is shot through the saddle and the bullet drives a nail into his thigh just as Pickett's Charge is being repulsed. He refuses to leave the field until the victory is certain. The wound ends his field command career. Simultaneously: Meade arriving too late, the pursuit question, and the Army of the Potomac's exhausted commanders.

placements.notes: Hancock commanding the Union center -- he has been everywhere on Cemetery Ridge all afternoon, riding the line
HANCOCK WOUNDED -- shot through the saddle. A nail and wood fragments driven into his thigh. He will not leave the field.
Sykes V Corps in reserve -- Meade's largest intact force, never ordered to pursue
Sedgwick's VI Corps -- 15,000 fresh men who fought almost nothing. Still in reserve.
Hancock still commanding despite wound -- he has tourniquet applied but stays until he sees the charge broken completely
Newton commanding I Corps remnants on Cemetery Hill -- the survivors of July 1
Howard's XI Corps -- battered from July 1, holding Cemetery Hill
Hancock finally carried from the field -- he sends Meade a note: the repulse is total and the enemy is retreating
Buford's cavalry -- Meade has not ordered pursuit. Buford's horses are exhausted.
VI Corps still in reserve -- Meade deliberating. The window for pursuit is closing.
More VI Corps in reserve -- 27000 fresh men standing by while Lee's army retreats
Gibbon now commanding II Corps -- Hancock in the ambulance. The corps that stopped Pickett exhausted.
Longstreet's corps on Seminary Ridge -- waiting for the Union pursuit that does not come
Hills corps covering the Confederate retreat -- also waiting for the blow that does not fall
VI Corps -- Meade has decided not to pursue today. Lincoln will be devastated. The war will continue two more years.
